content: 1. Depression has been studied in the context of health locus of control, as published in the Journal of Clinical Nursing in August 2014. 2. Norouzi et al. investigated the effects of kangaroo care and music therapy on reducing maternal state anxiety, as reported in Complementary Therapies in Medicine in October 2013. 3. Rabiei et al. explored the impact of the Fordyce Happiness Program on postpartum depression, with findings published in the Journal of Research in Medical Sciences in March 2014. 4. Rahman et al. conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial in rural Pakistan, demonstrating the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy-based interventions delivered by community health workers to mothers with depression and their infants. This study was published in The Lancet in September 2008. 5. Rojas et al. evaluated the treatment of postnatal depression in low-income mothers attending primary care clinics in Santiago, Chile, through a randomized controlled trial, as detailed in The Lancet in November 2007. 6. Salehi et al. compared group cognitive behavioral therapy with interactive lectures in reducing anxiety during pregnancy in a quasi-experimental trial, published in Medicine in October 2016. 7. Tripathy et al. assessed the effects of participatory interventions with women’s groups on birth outcomes and maternal depression in India through a cluster-randomized controlled trial, as reported in The Lancet. 8. Zhao et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of a prenatal depression intervention on perinatal outcomes among high-risk pregnant women in China, with results published in Archives of Women’s Mental Health in April 2017. 9. Maselko et al. followed up on the Thinking Healthy Program, a randomized controlled trial, to assess the long-term impact of early perinatal depression interventions on child development outcomes, as published in The Lancet Psychiatry in 2015. 10. Aboud et al. examined the effectiveness of a parenting program in Bangladesh aimed at improving early childhood health, growth, and development, with findings published in Social Science & Medicine in November 2013. 11. Akbarzadeh et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to teach attachment behaviors to pregnant women and evaluated its effects on infant mental health from birth to three months, as reported in Annals of Saudi Medicine in May 2016. 12. Attanasio et al. utilized the infrastructure of a conditional cash transfer program in Colombia to deliver a scalable early childhood development program, with results published in BMJ in September 2014. 13. Baker-Henningham et al. investigated the impact of early stimulation on maternal depression through a cluster-randomized controlled trial, as detailed in Archives of Disease in Childhood in December 2005. 14. Chang et al. integrated a parenting intervention with routine primary health care in a cluster-randomized trial, with findings published in Child in August 2015. 15. Çiftçi and Arikan studied the effects of training programs for working mothers on maternal anxiety levels and breastfeeding habits, as reported in the Journal of Clinical Nursing in August 2012. 16. Clarke et al. analyzed the impact of participatory interventions with women’s groups on psychological distress among mothers in rural Bangladesh, as a secondary analysis of a cluster-randomized controlled trial, published in PLOS One in October 2014. 17. Cooper et al. conducted a pilot study on the impact of a mother-infant intervention in a peri-urban South African context, with findings published in BJPsych in January 2002. 18. Cooper et al. also evaluated a randomized controlled trial aimed at improving the quality of mother-infant relationships and infant attachment in socioeconomically deprived communities in South Africa, as published in BMJ in April 2009. 19. Ho et al. assessed the effectiveness of a discharge education program in reducing the severity of postpartum depression through a randomized controlled evaluation study, as reported in Patient Education and Counseling in October 2009. 20. Le Roux et al. evaluated the outcomes of home visits for pregnant mothers and their infants in a cluster-randomized controlled trial, with findings published in AIDS (London, England) in June 2013. 21. Morris et al. examined whether combining infant stimulation with emergency feeding improved psychosocial outcomes for displaced mothers and babies in northern Uganda, as reported in the American Journal of Orthopsychiatry in July 2012. 22. Rahman et al. conducted a cluster-randomized trial of a parent-based intervention to support early child development in a low-income country, with findings published in Child: Care, Health and Development in January 2009. 23. Shariat and Abedini investigated the effects of psychological interventions on mother-infant bonding and breastfeeding, as reported in the Iranian Journal of Neonatology in 2017. 24. Shrestha et al. developed and evaluated a newborn care education program for first-time mothers in Nepal, with findings published in Midwifery in November 2016. 25. Singla et al. assessed the effects of a parenting intervention on maternal psychological well-being and child development in rural Uganda through a community-based, cluster-randomized trial, as reported in The Lancet Global Health in August 2015.
